content.jointProblem: Can a site-specific groundwater monitoring network and a passive/containment-based leachate remediation proposal be designed for Zelena Petlja's unlined temporary storage yard within the inspectorate's 120-day deadline, using existing data plus a targeted field campaign to test seasonal flow and leachate transport assumptions?

rationale.text: Zorić is explicitly open to contract research on site-specific leachate transport modelling and containment design, which matches the core task.

sources.quote: contract research on site-specific leachate transport modelling and containment design

rationale.text: She has consulting experience in groundwater monitoring programme design and interceptor drain performance assessment at operational landfills.

sources.quote: provided technical consulting to Ekološki Inženjering Panonija d.o.o. between 2016 and 2018 on groundwater monitoring programme design and interceptor drain performance assessment

rationale.text: She has field experience monitoring leachate in a northern Vojvodina alluvial aquifer with an 18-piezometer network and has recommended dual-tracer compliance monitoring.

sources.quote: A closed landfill in northern Vojvodina was monitored over a 30-month period using a network of 18 piezometers
recommends dual-tracer campaigns for compliance monitoring at comparable sites

rationale.text: She has published design charts for passive interceptor drains as a containment alternative at small municipal landfills.

sources.quote: Passive interceptor drains placed perpendicular to groundwater flow are a cost-effective alternative to pump-and-treat systems at small municipal landfills
dimensionless design charts for drain spacing, penetration depth, and gravel-pack hydraulic conductivity ratio

rationale.text: She has studied seasonal water-table controls on leachate infiltration at a municipal transfer station, directly relevant to the yard's unknown seasonal flow conditions.

sources.quote: monitored water table levels at 15-minute intervals over 24 months using pressure transducers installed in six piezometers around a municipal transfer station in Novi Sad
containment designs based solely on mean annual conditions may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40 % in this climatic setting

rationale.text: She has reviewed leachate-hydrogeology chapters of environmental impact studies for Vojvodina waste-facility permit applications, supporting the inspectorate-facing proposal.

sources.quote: reviewed environmental impact study chapters on leachate hydrogeology for several municipal waste facility permit applications in Vojvodina

rationale.text: Her project work includes dense piezometer networks and region-specific passive containment design guidelines for Vojvodina waste facilities.

sources.quote: installation of a dense piezometer network at four representative sites
development of region-specific passive containment design guidelines

constraints.text: The collaboration must produce four groundwater monitoring wells and a remediation proposal within the inspectorate's 120-day order, before late June 2024.

sources.quote: issued an order requiring us to install four groundwater monitoring wells within 120 days and to submit a remediation proposal
all before the 120-day deadline runs out in late June 2024

constraints.text: The plan must start from sparse recent hydrogeological information: only a 1993 sketch exists, and both contamination extent and seasonal flow direction are unknown.

sources.quote: We have a hydrogeological sketch from when the site was first permitted in 1993 but nothing more recent.
We do not know how far the contamination has moved or which direction groundwater flows under the site at different seasons.

constraints.text: Containment design must assume the yard liner is not a liquid-retention barrier; liner defects can greatly increase groundwater loading under wet conditions.

sources.quote: The liner under that area was never designed for liquid retention.
a 50 mm circular defect increased cumulative groundwater loading by 340 % relative to an intact liner under wet antecedent conditions

constraints.text: Analytical and staffing capacity is limited to a basic wet-chemistry bench and two process technicians, with no dedicated research budget or laboratory.

sources.quote: no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond the basic wet-chemistry bench used for leachate monitoring
two technicians with process engineering backgrounds who track sorting-line performance data daily

constraints.text: Seasonal water-table variation must be designed for; mean-annual assumptions can underestimate peak leachate infiltration by up to 40% in this climatic setting.

sources.quote: containment designs based solely on mean annual conditions may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40 % in this climatic setting

constraints.text: The remediation proposal should use site-specific geochemical attenuation evidence where relevant, because attenuation factors are expected in Serbian landfill permit assessments.

sources.quote: reporting geochemical attenuation factors as part of site-specific risk assessments for Serbian landfill permit applications

risks: Researcher availability for the 2024 120-day deadline is unknown; the only availability evidence refers to a reduced teaching load in 2025/26.

Her leachate-transport evidence comes from closed landfills, a transfer station and gravel/alluvial aquifer studies; applying it to an unlined temporary storage yard with high COD and unknown flow is a transfer gap to test in the first field campaign.
The 120-day deadline leaves little time for seasonal monitoring; the study that addressed seasonality used 24 months of water-table monitoring.
The company states no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond a basic wet-chemistry bench, which may constrain drilling, laboratory analysis and model calibration.

Her passive-treatment evidence focuses on ammonium removal by zeolite PRBs; it does not demonstrate treatment of 3,400 mg/L COD leachate, so the treatment proposal may need additional processes and pilot testing.
The inspectorate's acceptance criteria for well design and remediation proposal content are not specified, so regulatory sign-off remains a risk.
questions: Can Zorić confirm availability and field capacity for the 120-day window ending late June 2024, given her teaching load and project commitments?
What exactly does the inspectorate order require for the four wells (locations, depths, construction, sampling frequency) and what remediation-proposal format or standards will be accepted?
What existing site data can be shared: the 1993 hydrogeological sketch, borehole logs, water levels, leachate sampling QA/QC, waste composition, yard drainage, liner condition and topography?
What budget and procurement route exist for drilling, laboratory analyses and any treatment pilot, given the stated lack of a dedicated research budget?
What are the leachate flow/volume, COD/ammonium/heavy-metal concentrations beyond the single COD value, and any seasonal water-table data?
Will the company provide site access, technician time and permission for data use or publication, and what IP terms would apply?
Can external funding or a joint project application cover the work, and how would that timeline fit the 120-day regulatory deadline?
